seed.text: Engineering and controlling quantum dynamics to build scalable, programmable quantum systems.
Understanding how complex quantum dynamics, entanglement, criticality, and information give rise to emergent physical structure—from many-body phases to spacetime and gravity.

Understanding the fundamental relationship between quantum structure and computational power: which properties of quantum states and dynamics constitute genuine computational resources, how those resources can be encoded and manipulated, and under what conditions they yield provable computational advantage.

Understanding what quantum correlations fundamentally permit and forbid: how the geometry and structure of the quantum state space impose limits on information, communication, randomness, and correlations—and how those uniquely quantum resources can be operationally harnessed.

Understanding and engineering how collective quantum phenomena emerge from, interact with, and can be controlled through the coupled dynamics of matter, electromagnetic fields, and mechanical excitations.

Understanding how quantum information can be encoded into collective, nonlocal structures so that it becomes robust against local physical errors, and how those protected structures can be made computationally and physically realizable.
